metadata.title: Suno, Part One.
metadata.audience: HAI Lyrical Literacy volunteers — zero music or AI background. Internal training, not promotion.
metadata.narration_notes: Host is Rohan V. Name is spoken EXACTLY ONCE, in BOUT. Phonetic spellings are deliberate for Kokoro G2P: 'Rohaan' = Row-Haan. Do not 'correct' them to the normal spelling. Register is internal volunteer training — never promotional. Pro access is stated once, mechanically, in B03; HAI's provision of it is never sold.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Rohaan from Humanitarians AI. This is the first of three training videos on Suno for Lyrical Literacy volunteers. This one covers a single task: making your first song. You don't need a music background, and you don't need to have used an AI tool before. Work along with me and you'll finish with a complete track.

The ask types itself into the composer, character by character
Send button arms terracotta; running indicator appears
Three result lines reveal in sequence — the three steps of the video

props.command: Walk me through making my first song with Suno — I've never done this before.
props.runningText: setting up your Lyrical Literacy session…
output: Step 1: Sign in at suno.com with Discord.
Step 2: Describe the song — style, mood, topic.
Step 3: Click Create. Two versions come back in about a minute.

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. You type a sentence describing the song you want. Suno returns a finished track — vocals, melody, instruments, arrangement. It is not stitching together existing recordings; it generates new audio every time. Everything else in this video is detail on how to write that sentence and where to click.

shot.new_visual_element: SourceFlow pipeline — description → Suno → finished track with live waveform

show.event: A description card types in on the left
Arrow draws right into the Suno node; node pulses
Output card resolves on the right with an animated waveform
Stem labels — Vocals, Melody, Instruments — stack under the waveform

beats.narration_text: Suno is a generative model trained on a very large catalogue of music. In training it learned the patterns linking words to sound — what makes a track read as folk rather than hip-hop, hopeful rather than tense. Given your description it predicts audio that fits, a segment at a time, each segment continuing from the one before it. That is why the same prompt never returns quite the same song twice.

shot.new_visual_element: Genre corpus → learned mapping → segment-by-segment autoregressive generation

show.event: Genre chips stream in from the left edge into the model node
Word→sound mapping pairs light up: 'folk'→sparse waveform, 'hip-hop'→dense waveform
Generation strip builds left to right, one segment at a time, each keyed to the last
Two different waveforms render from one identical prompt — the non-determinism point

beats.narration_text: First, get signed in. Join the Humanitarians AI Discord — your team lead has the invite. Go to suno dot com and click Sign In. Choose Discord as your sign-in method: that is what links your account to the organisation's Pro plan. Use the same Discord account you joined with. Pro access applies automatically once you are in.

shot.new_visual_element: Four-step sign-in sequence — plain procedural checklist

show.event: Step cards slide in from the left, stacked
Step 1 highlights terracotta as narration reaches it
Steps complete with a check mark as the voice moves on
Final step lands; Pro badge resolves quietly beneath

props.sparkLine: Four steps. Then you are in.

beats.narration_text: This is the workspace. The left sidebar is how you move around it, and four items matter today. Home is a feed of recent activity. Explore shows what other people have published — useful for hearing how a description turns into sound. Library holds every track you generate, saved automatically. And Create is where you make songs. That is where we are going.

shot.new_visual_element: Full Suno application window — sidebar navigation walked item by item

show.event: Suno window resolves: sidebar, top bar, content grid with track rows
Home highlights; content area shows the feed state
Create highlights; callout names it as the working page
Library highlights; saved tracks with waveforms slide in
Explore highlights; published community tracks fill the grid

beats.narration_text: The Create page has three tabs: Simple, Advanced and Sounds. Advanced is where you control lyrics and song structure — that is Part 2. Stay on Simple. Three things matter here: the Song Description box, the Instrumental toggle for a track with no vocals, and the Create button at the bottom. That is the entire interface for your first song.

shot.new_visual_element: Suno Create page — Simple/Simple/Advanced/Sounds tabs, description box, instrumental toggle, Create button

show.event: Create page resolves inside the Suno window
Simple / Simple/Advanced/Sounds tab group highlights; Simple is active
Description box outlines terracotta; prompt text types in
Instrumental toggle flicks on then off, showing what it does
Create button arms

beats.narration_text: Write your description with three ingredients. Style: what genre or sound — folk, pop, hip-hop. Mood: what the music should feel like — hopeful, playful, calm. Topic: what the song is actually about. Put together: a gentle acoustic folk song, warm and hopeful, about children discovering the joy of reading. Style, mood, topic. That is a complete description.

shot.new_visual_element: Three ingredient cards assembling into one complete prompt sentence

show.event: Style card lands and fills with its example words
Mood card lands beside it
Topic card lands third
Cards resolve downward into the assembled sentence, each fragment tinted to its source card

beats.act: Act 7 — generating, and what it costs
beats.narration_text: Click Create. Suno generates two versions at once, usually in thirty to sixty seconds. Each generation costs five credits. The Pro plan carries two thousand five hundred credits a month — about five hundred songs — so you can afford to iterate rather than trying to get it right on the first attempt.

shot.new_visual_element: Create pressed → two generation slots fill with progressive waveforms → credit ledger ticks

show.event: Create button depresses; two empty generation slots appear
Progress sweeps across both slots; waveforms draw in as they complete
Elapsed timer counts up through the 30–60 second band
Credit ledger deducts 5 and shows the monthly balance remaining

beats.narration_text: Two cards appear, one per version. Press play and listen to both — they interpret the same description differently, and comparing them tells you what your wording actually did. The three-dot menu on each card holds what you can do next — Remix, Edit, Share and Download, each opening its own set of choices. Download, then MP3, is how you save the file.

shot.new_visual_element: Two finished song cards with playing waveforms; three-dot menu opens with real Suno actions

show.event: Two song cards resolve side by side, each with artwork and a waveform
Play presses on card one; its waveform animates and a progress line sweeps
Card two plays; its waveform differs visibly from card one
Three-dot control highlights and the real ten-item menu opens, submenu carets visible
Remix and Edit highlight in turn as named, then Download

props.sparkLine: Compare the two. That is the lesson.

beats.narration_text: To review. Sign in at suno dot com with Discord. Open Create and stay on Simple. Describe the song as style, mood and topic in one sentence. Press Create and wait about a minute for two versions. Use the three-dot menu to extend, remix or download. Five credits a generation, against two thousand five hundred a month.

beats.narration_text: That is the first pass. We covered what Suno is doing underneath, how to get signed in, how the workspace is laid out, the three-ingredient description, and how to read the two versions you get back. Part 2 goes deeper on the description itself — how wording changes the output, and when to move from Simple to Advanced mode.
